text:
Kiran Patel: Re-opening the resume-lite discussion — want final decisions on eviction, tenant quotas, and billing before I update the RFC.

Marie Lopez: Short version of my ask: how do we surface "resume failed" to the user, and how does billing avoid counting the prefix twice?

Kiran Patel: Proposal: token remains thin (opaque id + checksum). Edge stores a tiny checkpoint in an ephemeral store keyed by tenant. If checkpoint evicted -> we return a trailer flag `resume:lost` and do a cold retry path. Billing: annotate checkpoint with `billing.token_ts` and only charge suffix tokens once resume confirmed.

Samir Rao: Implementation constraints: keep per-entry footprint small. We cannot keep full KV caches per entry. Suggest storing a canonicalized runtime cursor (sequence id + kvcache signature) instead of full buffers. Eviction policy: LRU per-tenant with TTL 60s.

Anya K: Client UX: we should send a trailer with `{progress: enum, prefix_tokens:int, message:string}`. Clients that see `progress:lost` can surface a retry hint. I'll sketch proto.

Jim O'Neill: Fairness: shard resume-store by tenant and enforce `resume.active_limit` (configurable). If tenant over limit, return early hint header `X-RW-Resume-Denied: quota` so upstream clients can fallback. Emit metric `resume.denied.tenant=<id>`.

Marie Lopez: For billing flow: finance needs a contract. If resume successful, mark checkpoint settled and bill only delta. If lost, bill full tokens from cold retry path. We need idempotency keys to avoid double-charges if a client replays after a transient.

Kiran Patel: Retry budget: introduce `X-RW-Retry-Budget` header that proxies decrement. If budget reaches 0, proxies stop hedging. That avoids cross-layer explosion.

Samir Rao: Edge behavior on eviction: two options — synchronous lookup (adds tail latency) or optimistic fast-fail to cold retry. Suggest client opt-in via header; default is fast-fail (no resume) to preserve RTT-sensitive callers.

Anya K: Agree on opt-in. Also propose `x-rw-resume-wait-ms` optional header so client can say how long it's willing to wait for resume lookup.

Kiran Patel: Example request (docs draft):

```
curl -H "X-RW-Resume-Token: r_83abf" \n     -H "X-RW-Retry-Budget: 2" \n     -H "X-RW-Tenant-ID: tenant-55" \n     https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/generate --no-buffer
```

gateway-bot: Canary checklist: feature flag `edge.resume_opt_in`, rollout segments (5/20/100 tenants), metrics: `resume.success`, `resume.evicted`, `resume.denied`, `resume.lookup_latency_p50/p95`, `resume.billing.settled`.

Jim O'Neill: Ops note: surface `resume.store.utilization{tenant}` in console and add alert when utilization > 85% for a tenant. We should also provide per-tenant quota bump workflow.

Marie Lopez: Finance will want clear logs linking checkpoint IDs to billing events. Samir, can your store include a stable `checkpoint_id` we can reference in billing records?

Samir Rao: Yes — store will return `checkpoint_id` and `created_ts`. We'll persist minimal bookkeeping for billing settlement (not full checkpoint payload).

Anya K: I'll add the trailer proto draft and sample client handling patterns (opt-in, wait-ms, how to surface lost progress).

Kiran Patel: Action items: Samir: design store API + TTL/eviction; Marie: billing contract draft; Anya: trailer proto + client guidance; Jim: console metrics + deny path; I'll collate and update the RFC with headers and rollout plan.

Kiran Patel: One more: add a tracing tag `rw.resume.cache_state=hit|miss|evicted` so we can correlate latency and billing anomalies.

gateway-bot: Noted — will add trace tag checklist to the rollout doc.

Marie Lopez: Thanks — pushing for clarity before we flip the feature flag.

Kiran Patel: Thanks all. I’ll open a follow-up PR with concrete header names, sample curl, and canary steps. :rocket:
